diagnostic_evidence.quote: complemented by a BP limiter to ensure the BP property of partial densities, pressure, and volume fraction.
Next, enforce the pressure positivity $p \ge \varepsilon_p$ with $\varepsilon_p = \min\{ p(\overline{\mathbf{U}}_{i,j}^n), 10^{-13} \}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The kappa-step changes z1 while (rho e) is frozen, and the pressure depends on z1 through gamma and p_w. Theorem thm:implicit_solver bounds only z1. Use the paper's gas-water parameters (gamma1=1.4, pw1=0; gamma2=4.4, pw2=6000) and take z1=0.9, p=1, u=0. Then rho e is about 778.75, and z1=0.89 at the same rho e gives p of about -33. The derivative p'(z1) is large, so p(z1)>0 only for z1 >~ 0.8997. With kappa about 0.1 and compression D<0, F>0 on [0.8997,0.9] once |D|Delta t_im >~ 0.003, so any root has p<=0. After projection p(Ubar) can be negative. Step 2 then takes eps_p=min{p(Ubar),1e-13}<0 and cannot restore p>0. No cell-average admissibility analysis is given for the transport step either. The claimed unconditional BP (G^p, including pressure) is therefore not established.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified. At minimum, a repair must redesign the kappa-step, or couple it with the energy/pressure, so that the updated cell averages stay in G^p. It must also prove weak positivity of the transport-step cell averages under an explicit CFL condition.
issues.overall_effect: Pressure positivity, and hence membership in G^p, is not guaranteed in the stiff gas-liquid regime the paper targets. The abstract and introduction claims of unconditional BP and stable operation under a standard CFL are unsupported.
issues.title: Implicit kappa-step does not preserve pressure positivity; BP of the scheme in G^p is unestablished
issues.why_classification: The headline BP guarantee for pressure fails in the advertised regime. Restoring it needs a new update and new analysis, or a time-step restriction that defeats the 'unconditional' claim.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: BP property of \eqref{adaptive_sdirk2} is similar to the proof of Theorem \ref{thm:implicit_solver}, so omitted.

issues.failure_explanation: With (rho e)^n frozen, p(z1) sweeps values in (-pw2,-pw1) over [0,1]; for example z1^n=0.9, p=1 gives p(0) of about -23750. Write a_k=gamma_k(p+pw_k), so kappa=z1 z2(a2-a1)/(z1 a2+z2 a1). In the band -6000<p<0 we have a1<0<a2. The denominator (equivalently nu) is positive as p->0- and negative as p->-6000+, while the numerator stays positive. Hence kappa, f and F have a pole inside (0,1). F is not continuous on [0,1]: the signs F(0)<=0<=F(1) can come from the jump across the pole, so the IVT yields no root, and bisection may converge to the pole. Appendix A itself exhibits nu<0 for such mixtures.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified. At minimum, a repair must establish continuity of F on [0,1] along the root search (nu nonzero, p+pw_k>0), or modify the update (e.g. evaluate nu_k at the admissible p^n so kappa is continuous). It must then reprove existence in [0,1] for both implicit variants.
issues.overall_effect: Unconditional existence of a bounded implicit solution is unproven for backward Euler and for the adaptive SDIRK2 scheme, whose BP proof is deferred to this one. The bisection solver is not justified.
issues.title: IVT existence proof assumes continuity of F, but kappa has a pole in (0,1)
issues.why_classification: The central unconditional-BP theorem for the implicit solver fails as proved. Fixing it requires changing the scheme or adding a new argument that the source does not supply.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The solution after BP limiter satisfies \eqref{U_ingp} and maintain the element average of the OEDG solution.

issues.failure_explanation: The formula theta_p=(pbar-eps)/(pbar-p_min) yields p>=eps only if p is concave along segments from Ubar. Here p=N(U)/D(z1), with N concave but D affine in z1 and varying along the segment. Thus p(theta) is at best the D-weighted average [(1-theta)Dbar pbar+theta D~ p_min]/[(1-theta)Dbar+theta D~], with equality when u=0. Take pbar=1, p_min=-1 and eps about 0. Then theta is about 1/2 and the limited pressure is about (Dbar-D~)/(Dbar+D~), which is negative whenever the minimizing point has a larger gas fraction (D~>Dbar).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Compute theta_p from the concave function g(U)=N(U)-eps_p D(U) (theta=gbar/(gbar-min g)), or solve exactly for theta. Both are standard and local.
issues.overall_effect: The stated pointwise guarantee U in G^p at quadrature points after the BP limiter can fail even when cell averages are admissible.
issues.title: Linear-scaling pressure limiter does not guarantee p >= eps_p
issues.why_classification: This is a routine local change to the limiter formula that preserves the method and its claims.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the resulting temporal error remains subdominant to the overall error.
For all cases, we simply employ $\Delta t \propto \Delta x$ and $CFL=0.1$.
In this work, we implicitly solve it in first-order backward Euler:
preserving high-order fidelity in the smooth, single-phase regions.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper concedes O(Delta t^2) temporal error. It is only first order where backward Euler is used, as in the written Strang steps and the SDIRK2 fallback. With Delta t proportional to Delta x the error is O(Dx^{K+1})+O(Dx^2), so for P2 the temporal part must dominate asymptotically, and third order is not 'expected'. The localization remark does not apply: in the smooth test z1 lies in (0.1,0.9) everywhere, so the kappa-step is active globally, and interface errors are transported anyway. The observed rates are pre-asymptotic or empirical only.

failure_location.quote: still exhibits the expected third-order convergence.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the accuracy as at most second order in time. Run the P2 convergence tests with Delta t proportional to Delta x^{3/2} (or report asymptotic rates), and remove the localization claim.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed high-order (third-order for P2) accuracy of the Kapila-split scheme is unsupported. The scheme is asymptotically at most second order, and first order where backward Euler is used.
issues.title: Third-order accuracy claimed with Delta t proportional to Delta x despite an O(Delta t^2) splitting error
issues.why_classification: An advertised accuracy order must be withdrawn and the tests redone. This is a limited weakening and needs no new architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: G requires z1 rho1>0 and z2 rho2>0 strictly. U^(1) has z2 rho2=0 and U^(2) has z1 rho1=0, so neither endpoint lies in G, and the stated counterexample does not show that G is non-convex.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Perturb the endpoints to small positive partial densities with z1 slightly inside (0,1). Since c^2(U^(s))<0 strictly and the endpoint c^2 stay positive, continuity preserves the counterexample.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed demonstration that G is non-convex, which motivates replacing G by G^p, is invalid as written.
issues.title: Appendix A counterexample endpoints violate the strict inequalities defining G
issues.why_classification: A short continuity or perturbation argument restores the claim unchanged.
